rules: All figures containing LHCb data must show the label "LHCb" ("LHCb preliminary" for preliminary results, "LHCb simulation" for simulation-only figures), and figures that do not depend on LHCb-specific software should have no label.
Figures containing LHCb data must show the corresponding integrated luminosity (e.g. "9 fb^-1" on a new line under "LHCb"), or the centre-of-mass energy for cross-section or heavy-ion papers.
Figures must be legible at the size they will appear in the publication, with suitable line widths.
Axes must be labelled with suitable units, chosen so the tick numbers do not run together (e.g. GeV/c^2 rather than MeV/c^2 for a range of several GeV/c^2).

The y-axis should read "Entries" or "Candidates" without background subtraction, or "Yield" or "Decays" with it, and should state the bin width when it shows a per-bin yield, e.g. "Entries / (5 MeV/c^2)".
Axis labels and legends should use the same text font as the main text, with upright symbols, or consistently upright sans-serif throughout, but styles must not be mixed.
Particle symbols in figures should use the same roman or italic font as in the text.
Minus signs in figure labels must be proper minus signs, not hyphens.
Colour may be used, but differently coloured lines and areas must stay distinguishable in black-and-white print, for example through different dash styles.
Never use a rainbow palette for two-dimensional plots, and use printer-friendly, colour-blind-safe palettes instead.
Filled areas should use different hatching styles to stay distinguishable in black and white, avoiding hatch styles that behave unpredictably when zoomed or scaled.
Fit curves must not hide the data points, which are best drawn on top of the fit curves.
Avoid spurious background shading and boxes around text, including legend frames.
Multi-part figures should label their parts (a), (b), etc. and describe each part in the caption, or refer to them clearly by position.

Captions go below the figure, should be short and correctly punctuated, use a slightly smaller typeface than the text, describe the data before the fit components, and should not start with an article or contain numbered equations.
Pull plots should normally not appear in papers unless they show regions where the fit does not describe the data.
Figure files must be in PDF format for pdflatex (EPS for plain LaTeX) and placed in the figs/ directory.
